rejected.title: The social-ecological model
card: The social-ecological model says a person's physical activity is shaped at four levels at once, not by personal choice alone. The first is the individual level: a person's own knowledge, skills, attitudes, confidence and motivation.
Social
the people around a person, such as family, friends, teammates and teachers, who can influence what they do.
Physical environment
the places and spaces a person can use, such as parks, footpaths, bike paths and pools, and their features, such as lighting or shade.
Policy
the rules, laws and funding decisions made by governments, schools and other organisations. A policy is the decision itself, not the place it may pay for.
rejected.remember: Promoting activity can target the person, the people around them, the places they use, or the rules and funding behind them.

a.q: Which example belongs to the social level of the model?
opts: A teenager's friends invite her to join a netball team
A teenager feels confident about her own ball skills
A new netball court opens in the park near her home
A state government funds free sport for all students
a.why: Friends are people around the teenager, so their influence sits at the social level. Confidence is a personal trait, so it is at the individual level. The court is a place, so it is the physical environment, and the funding decision is policy.
a.clue: Look for the option about other people around the person.

b.q: Few teenagers in Mildura use the local skate park. A survey finds it has no lighting, so it is unsafe after school. Which level is this problem at?
opts: Physical environment
Individual
Social
Policy
b.why: Lighting and safety are features of the place itself, so this is the physical environment. Individual is tempting, because teenagers choose not to go, but the cause is the setting, not their skills or attitudes. Policy would be a rule or funding decision, not the missing lights.
b.clue: Ask what feature of the place is causing the problem.

draft.title: The social-ecological model
card: The social-ecological model says a person's physical activity is shaped by several levels at once, not by personal choice alone.
Individual
a person's own traits, such as their knowledge, skills, attitudes, confidence and motivation.
Social
the people around a person, such as family, friends, teammates and teachers, who can influence what they do.
Physical environment and policy
the places and spaces available, such as parks, footpaths and pools, and the rules and funding set by governments and organisations.
draft.remember: Activity is shaped by many levels at once, so promoting it can target more than the person.

a.q: Which example belongs to the social level of the model?
opts: A teenager's friends invite her to join a netball team
A teenager feels confident about her ball skills
A council builds a new netball court in her suburb
A state government funds free sport for all students
a.why: Friends are people around the teenager, so their influence sits at the social level. Confidence is a personal trait, so it is at the individual level. The court is a place, and the funding is a policy.
a.clue: Look for the option about other people around the person.

b.q: Few teenagers in Mildura use the local skate park. A survey finds it has no lighting, so it is unsafe after school. Which level is this problem at?
opts: Physical environment
Individual
Social
Policy
b.why: Lighting and safety are features of a place, so this is the physical environment. It is tempting to say individual, because teenagers choose not to go. But the cause is the setting, not their own skills or attitudes.
b.clue: Ask what feature of the place is causing the problem.
